slides.heading: Combining Numbers and Variables
slides.body: Combining Numbers and Variables is part of Mathematical and String Operations. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Combining Numbers and Variables
slides.body: Variables can hold numbers and be used in calculations. This makes formulas easier to read and change.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Using variables in formulas is like writing a price tag and quantity on a receipt before calculating the total.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Python follows operator rules exactly. Use variables and parentheses to make calculations readable and predictable.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Create quantity and price variables, then print their product.

quiz.prompt_text: What is the advantage of using variables in calculations instead of just numbers?

options: It makes Python skip the calculation
It makes formulas easier to read and update
It automatically converts floats to integers

quiz.explanation: Well done! Using variables in calculations makes formulas more readable and easier to update — if a value changes, you only need to update it once.

quiz.prompt_text: Arrange the following lines in the correct order to calculate the total price of 6 apples at 10 each and print it.
quiz.explanation: Both variables must be assigned before they can be used in the calculation inside print().

quiz.prompt_text: Create quantity and price variables, then print the result of multiplying them together.

content.hint: Use print(quantity * price) after setting both values.

quiz.correct_answer: Any valid Python code that satisfies the prompt.
quiz.explanation: Set quantity = 5 and price = 20 for example, then print(quantity * price) gives 100. Variables make it easy to change the values later.
